name: Cylindropuntia

project_scope.selection_mode: approved Master Plant Pool genus framework
project_scope.canonical_installation: Both source-pool species require Approved Taxa Installer; no species installed by this lesson.
project_scope.native_range: Do not infer three-target-county PASS from inclusion.

shared_genus_characters.look_here_first: Find true cactus areoles with glochids on JOINTED CYLINDRICAL stem segments; measure a mature segment's diameter and count large spines per areole. Then check mature fruit surface.
shared_genus_characters.shared: Opuntioid cacti with cylindrical segmented stems (not flattened Opuntia pads), areoles producing glochids/spines/flowers, and fleshy fruits.

species_comparison_matrix.imbricata: Strongly raised, widely spaced, typically 2–5 cm
species_comparison_matrix.leptocaulis: Low linear ridges, often appearing as longitudinal wrinkles when dry

species_comparison_matrix.imbricata: Usually 8–15, sometimes up to 30; exceptional nearly spineless plants
Yellow, prominently tuberculate, roughly 24–45 mm long
species_comparison_matrix.leptocaulis: Usually smooth, yellow to scarlet, typically 9–15 mm long (occasionally longer)
species_comparison_matrix.priority: HIGH supporting; fruit color not sole separator

species_comparison_matrix.imbricata: Open shrub or small tree with thick joints
species_comparison_matrix.leptocaulis: Dense fine-branched shrub with pencil-thin joints

decision_sequence: LOOK HERE FIRST: verify areoles + cylindrical joints; distinguish from flat-pad Opuntia.
Measure stem segment width and inspect tubercle relief; thick, raised-tubercled segments suggest C. imbricata; pencil-thin, low-ridged segments suggest C. leptocaulis.
Count major spines at several mature areoles, then inspect mature fruit size and tubercles.
If a plant combines thin joints with unusually tuberculate fruits or intermediate spination, photograph measurements and request diagnostic review rather than forcing a name.
overlap_and_cautions: Stem age, stress, and exceptional spineless plants can alter spine expression; do not use a single areole.
Fruit color varies in C. leptocaulis; yellow alone does not mean C. imbricata.
Hybridization is documented within Cylindropuntia; intermediates require reproductive evidence and review.
Both are approved source-pool concepts, not yet canonical learner species cards; do not treat index counts as installation proof.

lookalike_matrix.separate: Flattened pads rather than cylindrical jointed stems; both have areoles and glochids.
Narrow stems but more pronounced tubercles than C. leptocaulis; mature fruit and flowers plus locality needed; not a source-pool admission.

diagnostic_photo_checklist.shot: Both species, measured intact mature stem segments with mm ruler
Side-lit matched macros with areoles, spine counts and tubercle ridges labeled
Mature fruit side profiles with scale; label smooth vs tuberculate surfaces
Whole-plant branching comparison including woody trunk or shrub base
Flower and pericarpel areoles as reproductive confirmation, not color-based ID

visual_status: provisional_text_framework_only; no exact photos acquired; Diagnostic Photo Polish owns images

workflow_handoffs.installer: Install C. imbricata and C. leptocaulis through Approved Taxa Installer after taxonomic identity checks.
workflow_handoffs.photo_polish: Find exact-species measured joint, areole and mature-fruit photos with full license/provenance; do not substitute generic cholla photos.
workflow_handoffs.taxonomy_review: Investigate atypical narrow-jointed or strongly tuberculate intermediates; retain unresolved identity without forcing species.
